item.title: Réglages: « Synchro des comptes dans iCloud » in an info bubble (#1065), no footer under « Verrouiller l’app » (#1066)
item.body:
Closes #1065
Closes #1066
Claim: cloud/i970-sonnet
Author model: Sonnet 5.5 (cloud/i970-sonnet)
Reviewer model: Opus 5.5 (aed652e5f80d92f07, APPROVE on `184f23f`)

**Stacks on #1062 (PR #1064)**: it uses the `InfoBubbleButton` component that PR adds, so this branch carries its commits until #1062 merges; review only the last two commits (« Rename the iCloud account sync switch… » for #1065, « Remove the footer under « Verrouiller l’app » » for #1066). Once #1062 has merged, `dev-swift` is merged into this branch. ADR edit: cloud/orch merges this PR.

## Problem
- #1065: the iCloud account sync switch has a long title (« Synchroniser mes comptes via le trousseau iCloud ») and a paragraph under it, which makes the « Comptes » section long (operator feedback, 2026-11-17).
- #1066: « Sécurité » has a sentence under « Verrouiller l’app (Face ID / code) » that the switch makes obvious (same feedback).

## Cause
`SecuritySettingsSections` showed `AccountSyncMessages.explanation` and a fixed sentence as section footers.

## Change
- **#1065** `AccountSyncMessages.title` is « Synchro des comptes dans iCloud » (operator decision). The explanation moves **verbatim** (the operator reviewed it for #312) from the section footer into an info bubble: the shared `InfoBubbleButton` (an `info.circle` button with a popover kept as a bubble on iPhone) on the row; accessibility label « À propos de la synchro des comptes » (`AccountSyncMessages.infoLabel`). The switch-off reasons (`switchedOff`) and the error messages stay visible under the row (`accountSyncNotice`); the sync itself is untouched. Docs: the quoted name in LOT-173's spec and `LOTS.md` (and the generated `tooling/roadmap/lots.json`, from `lots_from_md.py`); ADR 0013 gets a dated sub-line « Renamed, 2026-11-17 (#1065) » under the bullet that quotes the old name, no rewrite of the decision.
- **#1066** the « Sécurité » footer (« L’app se verrouille au lancement… ») is removed. The switch, the « Verrouiller » delay picker and `lock.message` stay. No spec quotes the sentence (checked by grep), so no doc change.
- No `### Ledger`: SwiftHFR-only (GAP-168, GAP-169), no legacy behaviour.

## Tests
App tests (not runnable on Linux; compile-check, then CI):
- `AccountSyncMessagesTests.theSwitchHasTheShortName`: the new title. Fails without the change.
- `AccountSyncMessagesTests.theExplanationIsUnchanged`: the explanation equals the reviewed text, character for character (a literal copy of the original).
- `AccountSyncMessagesTests.theInfoButtonHasItsAccessibilityLabel`: the label the button uses.
- The lock tests are untouched and unaffected (the footer was a literal in the view).
- **Not covered by a test: « the explanation is in the popover, not under the row » (#1065) and « the section has no footer » (#1066).** The project has no view-inspection tool, and a popover's content is not in the hosted view's accessibility tree until it is presented; a hosted UI test is not something I can write or run without a Mac. Both hold by the code (the two `footer:` closures are gone; the explanation is built only in the `InfoBubbleButton` closure) and are left to the device check. The reviewer accepted this deviation; it is recorded on #1065 and #1066.

## Device check (for the #893 general review)
- Réglages › Comptes: the short title; a tap on (i) shows the explanation in a bubble (not a sheet) on iPhone; with the sync switched off by another device, its notice is still under the row.
- Réglages › Sécurité: no sentence under the switch.

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, aed652e5f80d92f07, head 184f23f4e4296792e49dc2b30be2eb403dedc0bf): APPROVE** — round 1, posted verbatim

**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, reviewer of #1067): APPROVE** — head 184f23f4

I reviewed only the commits stacked on #1064 (`origin/feat/1062-reply-button-description...184f23f4`).

**Findings**

1. **Low**: no view test for two acceptance criteria. `App/SwiftHFRTests/Accounts/AccountSyncMessagesTests.swift` only checks the three constants. Two criteria have no test: "the explanation is in the popover, not under the row" (#1065) and "the section has no footer" (#1066). If the explanation were put back as a `footer:`, every test would stay green. The PR's reason, "no view-inspection tool", is only partly true. The project does host views in tests (`ComposerPlacementSwitchHostedTests`, `ModernComposerOffHostedTests`), but those tests rely on preference-key markers placed in the production view. Building that setup to check that a footer is absent costs more than the risk of such a static layout change. I accept the deviation, on two conditions:
   - the author records it on #1065 and #1066;
   - the author adds the PR's "Device check" lines to #893, and keeps that as a to-do until it is done.
2. **Detail**: `docs/adr/0013-storage-tiers.md:74`. The dated "Renamed, 2026-11-17 (#1065)" line is the first item of the "Rules of the copy" list. It is not one of those rules, and the ADR otherwise records changes as `## Amendment N — date` sections. The issue asked for an amendment line, and this is one, so no change is needed. A future editor could move it to just after the bullet's lead sentence.

**Verified**
- I parsed both literals in Python (indentation stripped, `\` continuations joined). The explanation in `AccountsModel+Sync.swift` is byte-identical to the one on `origin/dev-swift`: the diff only touches doc comments. The test's literal equals the source's, including the typographic apostrophes (U+2019).
- `AccountSyncMessages.explanation` is used only inside the `InfoBubbleButton` closure.
- `accountSyncNotice` and `lock.message` are still shown under their rows. The toggle, the picker and `lock.message` of the Sécurité section are unchanged.
- I grepped the old title, "délai choisi" and "remplace Face ID" across the whole tree. The only hits left are deliberate "formerly" or "renamed from" mentions, plus ADR 0013:73, the decision text the issue said not to rewrite. GAP-168/169 do not quote the name. There is no localisation file.
- After `lots_from_md.py`, `lots.json` has no diff. `fold.py --check` and `check-lot-deps.py` pass.
- The Toggle and the borderless `InfoBubbleButton` in an `HStack` follow the `ReplyButtonRow` pattern: the button takes its own tap and does not flip the switch.
- PR body: `Closes #1065` and `Closes #1066`. Its `Claim: cloud/i970-sonnet` matches the claim on both issues. No `### Ledger` section is needed, since the feature is SwiftHFR-only.
- The ADR edit means cloud/orch merges this PR, as the body says.
- I could not run the app tests on Linux. CI Compile is green.

**Handled:** finding 1 — the deviation is recorded on #1065 and #1066, and the device-check lines go to #893 (hand-off comment, once #1064 is approved, since this PR stacks on it). Finding 2 — no change, as the reviewer says.

#1064 is merged; I merged `dev-swift` into this branch (head `00f5c88`).

**`--remerge-diff` is not empty**, so the earlier APPROVE does not carry over by the §8 rule. What the resolution is:
- The branch was stacked on the unsquashed #1062 commits, so two test files conflicted (`TopicReaderQuoteTests.swift`, `TopicsSettingsModelTests.swift`). I took `dev-swift`'s version of both (the merged #1064 content).
- The automatic merge also duplicated `ReplyButtonBehavior.isDefault` / `explanation` in `TopicsSettingsModel.swift` (it would not compile). Fixed in two follow-up commits by taking `dev-swift`'s file unchanged.
- Net diff vs `dev-swift` is now only this PR's 7 files (`AccountsModel+Sync`, `SecuritySettingsSections`, `AccountSyncMessagesTests`, `docs/LOTS.md`, ADR 0013, LOT-173, `lots.json`); no #1064 file differs.

Not built here (Linux). Needs the compile check on the new head, and a re-confirmation by the reviewer of the merge resolution before it is marked.

**Adversarial review (Opus 5.5, cloud/r1067-merge-opus, merge delta): APPROVE** — head 00f5c88

No findings. I checked only the merge resolution.

1. **Net diff against the merge base.** The merge base is `1eb1eadf`, the squash of #1064. `git diff 1eb1eadf 00f5c88d` touches exactly 7 files: `AccountsModel+Sync.swift`, `SecuritySettingsSections.swift`, the new `AccountSyncMessagesTests.swift`, `docs/LOTS.md`, ADR 0013, LOT-173 and `lots.json`. `TopicsSettingsModel.swift`, `SettingsView.swift`, `TopicReaderQuoteTests.swift` and `TopicsSettingsModelTests.swift` show no difference from dev-swift, so nothing of #1064 is reverted or duplicated.
2. **Remerge diff of `9287e236`.** It shows only the two expected conflicts, both resolved to dev-swift's side (#1064's longer doc comment and the renamed `theInfoButtonLabelIsThePinnedWording`). The resolution adds nothing else.
3. **No duplicates or stale references.** At the head, `isDefault` and `explanation` of `ReplyButtonBehavior` are each declared once (`TopicsSettingsModel.swift:62,67`). The other `infoLabel` and `explanation` declarations sit on separate types (`AccountSyncMessages`, `DefaultBrowserMessages`, `FilteredPostsMessages`, `ReplyButtonRow`, `MPDarkTopic`, `ExperimentalFeature`), so none collide. `InfoBubbleButton` is defined once (`Settings/InfoBubbleButton.swift:6`, `init(label:bubble:)`). The call in `SecuritySettingsSections.swift` matches that signature and passes a `Text`, so it compiles on a careful reading.
4. **`SettingsView.swift`.** It is identical to dev-swift's: #1064's rows are intact, and this PR's changes live in `SecuritySettingsSections`.
5. **Earlier review content.** It is unaffected. The PR's own changes (the switch rename, the bubble, the removed « Verrouiller l'app » footer from `184f23f4`, #1066) are byte-identical to before the merge.
6. **Current dev-swift.** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/dev-swift 00f5c88d`, with dev-swift at `0204b40c`, gives a clean tree with no conflicts. The two newer commits (#1091, #1092) do not touch `App/SwiftHFR/Settings` or `App/SwiftHFR/Accounts`.

**Checked by running:** `git show --remerge-diff 9287e236`, `git diff --stat` / `git diff` of the net diff and of the four shared paths, `git grep` at `00f5c88d` for the declarations and references, and `git merge-tree` against `origin/dev-swift`. I did not run Xcode, the tests or SwiftLint: this is Linux, and the delta changes no code against the earlier head beyond taking dev-swift's files.
